findings.ref: qg-cycle2/T-004/acceptance.log, Bash vs PowerShell named-SKIP text
findings.note: The twins emit non-identical named-SKIP text within the same acceptance log: Bash prints 'SKIP: F4/AC-007 (Epic A4 ): ...' with a trailing space inside the parenthesis (also '(Epic A1 )', '(A1+A6 )'), PowerShell prints '(Epic A4)', '(Epic A1)', '(A1+A6)'. Bash appends a separator per dependency while PowerShell joins them. No delivered assertion compares the two twins' SKIP lines, so nothing catches the drift. Harmless today, but AC-016/AC-027 require this exact line to become a fixed template string read from T-010's REQ-007 allowlist manifest; the divergence should be reconciled when T-010 re-points these SKIPs, or the manifest's fixed template will match one runtime and not the other.

findings.ref: design.md normalization algorithm step (3) vs the 40-assertion inventory and 44-case mutation inventory
findings.note: design.md fixes whitespace/line-ending normalization before either the frontmatter or heading comparison. The delivered assertion set contains only 'frontmatter order and permitted whitespace/line endings normalize', and the mutation set's whitespace cases both target the frontmatter value path. No named assertion or mutation covers heading-text horizontal-whitespace normalization. Impact is low (the failure mode is a false RED on a benign heading respacing, not a false GREEN), and the canonicalizer source is absent from the bundle so it cannot be confirmed whether heading text is in fact normalized - flagging the untested surface, not asserting a defect.

findings.ref: qg-cycle2/T-004/run-checks.sh critical-closure stage: echoed label vs the code that resolves the control
findings.note: The echoed label reads '--- C: PRE-FIX PowerShell twin from HEAD~1, identical condition ---' while the code resolves the control via 'git log --format=%H -- "$twin" | sed -n 2p'. The stage's own preamble explicitly documents that HEAD~1 was the off-by-one the seq0675 evaluator caught and that it was replaced. The stale label is now baked into the persisted critical-closure.log and would mislead a future auditor into thinking the discredited HEAD~1 resolution is still in use. Cosmetic, but it is evidence text, and evidence text that misstates its own method is worth correcting.
